analysis:
Support this exact candidate as an actionable architecture decision and bounded smoke-test plan, not transport qualification.

The boundary matches source/scripts/protocol.mjs: prepare reserves an attempt; record validates artifacts and recording-time deadlines; neither supervises execution. Keeping that API unchanged avoids implying that acceptance checks terminate work. The mandatory receipt, terminal-success prerequisite and unknown-cancellation/no-retry branch make responsibilities explicit without claiming executable enforcement.

The other expert’s strongest objection is that a concrete host must demonstrate lifecycle behavior before being advertised as supported. The candidate addresses it by explicitly leaving automatic deadline supervision and external CLI execution unqualified. Its reported interrupt/list_agents observation establishes, at most, an observed managed-turn interruption. It correctly excludes remote computation and descendant termination claims. These are coordinator-reported observations, not events I independently verified.

The strongest argument for a runner remains consequential: one executable owner could prevent acceptance after transport failure or retry before termination more reliably than coordinator instructions. Nevertheless, a CLI runner would not establish native-host guarantees and would add process-tree and provider-specific obligations. For this scope, withholding unsupported execution claims is smaller and more honest than building that runner.

High confidence: the artifact/process separation and failure contract are implementable from the supplied source and references. Lower confidence: any particular host’s unattended deadline behavior; the candidate does not claim that behavior has been proven. A controlled over-deadline task with dispatch, cancellation and terminal timestamps is the right discriminating experiment before expanding support claims.

The explicit preservation of the expired run, unchanged challenge digest and UNREVIEWED rule also prevents this consultation from turning agreement into runtime proof or retrospective endorsement.
concerns: Nonblocking dissent: coordinator-owned receipts and instructions remain weaker than an executable adapter; the helper will still accept a response without inspecting transport evidence.

The native success smoke test and reported interruption probe do not qualify automatic deadline supervision. Preserve that limitation prominently in the published decision and any supported-host guidance.

Unspecified receipt structure permits inconsistent evidence across hosts. This is acceptable initially, but repeated ambiguity in actual receipts would justify a small versioned schema before adding a general runner.
